sentences.text:
Shri Manish Yadav advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Vinod Thakur public prosecutor for State.
 Order
Learned counsel for the State submits that victim has duly been informed about filing of this bail application.

This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 880/2023 registered at Police Station-Manwar District- Dhar,(M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376,
376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 3,4,5(l)/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 16.01.2025.
Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in the matter under the pressure of family members of the victim.
She left her parental home at her own.
Victim was major at the time of alleged incident.
Victim and applicant lived at Morvi in Gujarat for one and half year where she delivered a girl child.
Learned counsel, further referring to evidence of victim (PW-1) and her father (PW-2) recorded before the trial Court, submits that both of them have exonerated the applicant of the alleged offence.

They stated that victim NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:12276 2 MCRC-19620-2025 was aged 19 years and presently, she is staying with the family of the applicant.
Material witness have been examined before the trial Court.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
However, after going through case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.
Allegedly, the applicant kidnapped minor victim aged around 16 years and 6 months and subjected her to penetrative sexual assault.
The victim got pregnant.
However, the victim and her father did not support the prosecution in evidence before the trial Court.
The veracity of the prosecution and age of victim will be determined after evidence at trial.
As informed, applicant is aged around 22 years at the time of his arrest.
He is labourer by profession.
He is still dependent on his family and surviving on occasional labour job.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.
In absence of any criminal antecedent, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence by the applicant.
The trial would take time to conclude.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the young applicant.
However, the observations, herein- above, are recorded for present application only.

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforesaid facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:12276 3 MCRC-19620-2025 inclined to release the applicant on bail.

Thus,
present application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Mukesh @ Kallu shall be released on bail in connection with the crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C. 1973/ Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023,
to secure presence of the applicant for the trial.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the Trial Court may consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
C.C. as per rules.
(SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR) JUDGE BDJ Mukesh@
